newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO year net jumps, plans share split.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO year net jumps, plans share split.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV on Thursday posted a 26 percent rise in 1996 net profit, but said that financial market uncertainties meant it was too early to forecast this year's results.
Total net profit rose to 3.30 billion guilders ($1.7 billion) from a previous 2.62 billion guilders ($1.4 billion), giving net per share of 9.26 guilders ($4.87) versus 7.69 guilders.
ABN, the Netherlands' biggest bank, will increase the dividend to 4.20 guilders per share from 3.60 guilders/share.
Analysts had expected net profit of between 3.27 billion guilders and 3.32 billion guilders.
ABN AMRO said it was optimistic on its outlook, but it was too early to make a forecast for current year results.
"The managing board looks forward to the future development of the bank with confidence.
"In the light of the uncertainties surrounding the financial markets, the board finds it too early to make a profit forecast for 1997," the bank said in a statement with 1996 results.
ABN, the largest foreign bank in the United States, also said it planned to list its shares in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) on the New York Stock Exchange.
As part of that arrangement, the bank will buy back one percent of its own shares to re-offer them to U.S. investors. The bank also announced plans for a four-for-one share split.
